## Burden of Proof
The responsibility to establish, to the required standard, that a crime occurred [bold]and[/bold] that a specific individual committed it. This burden rests with [bold]Security[/bold], not the accused.
For criminal proceedings, Security must establish guilt by a [bold]preponderance of available evidence[/bold] — meaning it is more likely than not, based on all available information, that the individual committed the offense.
### What Counts as Evidence
- Witness testimony - Physical evidence (weapons, stolen items, contraband) - Forensic evidence (medical scans, chemical analysis) - Security records and camera footage - Confessions and admissions - Investigative reports
### Key Principles
- The [bold]absence of direct evidence[/bold] does not automatically prevent a charge if the totality of available evidence reasonably supports it. - No individual shall be convicted on [bold]unsupported hearsay alone[/bold] — corroboration is required. - [bold]Contradictory or unreliable witness testimony[/bold] should be weighed against other available evidence. - The accused does [bold]not[/bold] have to prove their innocence — Security must prove guilt.
[bold][color=#ffffff]Example[/color][/bold]
No camera footage exists, but three independent witnesses report seeing the same individual attack a crew member unprovoked. The preponderance of evidence supports a charge of [textlink="101 — Assault" link="HLSpaceLawList"].
